config.title: Theme Context

intro.title: Theme Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue app that allows users to toggle between light and dark themes. You will learn how to use Vue's provide/inject API to create a theme context, which shares state across multiple components without passing props manually. The main technologies involved are Vue 3's Composition API, reactive state, and component communication patterns. By the end, you'll understand how to manage global UI state efficiently in a Vue application.
intro.usecase: Theme Context is a foundational pattern for managing consistent UI theming across entire applications. In real-world software, this is essential for implementing user-selectable light/dark modes in dashboards, admin panels, or productivity tools, where a single theme setting must propagate to all components like sidebars, cards, and modals. Developers use this to centralize theme logic—such as colors, fonts, and spacing—ensuring a cohesive look without manually passing props through every component layer. This pattern also supports dynamic theme switching, allowing users to personalize interfaces in applications like design tools or content management systems.

objectives: Initialize a reactive theme state using Vue's composition API
Construct a provider component to distribute theme context to child components
Implement a custom hook to consume theme context within components
Configure dynamic styling by binding theme values to component templates
Update theme state through user interactions like toggle buttons
Integrate theme context across multiple components in a Vue application
Manipulate component appearance based on the active theme context

steps.title: Import Vue and createApp
steps.instruction: Import Vue and createApp from the Vue CDN or module.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and its createApp function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing from a module
import { createApp } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary imports to start building a Vue application.
successCriteria: Vue and createApp are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and createApp from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import Vue and createApp from the Vue module.

steps.title: Create and export a reactive theme object
steps.instruction: Create a reactive theme object with properties like primaryColor and backgroundColor, and export it so it can be imported elsewhere.
steps.hint: Use Vue's reactive() function to create a reactive object. Define properties like primaryColor and backgroundColor with string values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive theme object is created and exported, ready to be used as a shared data source.
successCriteria: A reactive theme object with properties like primaryColor and backgroundColor is created and exported.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to use reactive() and include properties like primaryColor and backgroundColor.
steps.feedbackWrong: The theme object should be created with reactive() and have properties like primaryColor and backgroundColor. Try again.

steps.title: Create a provide function for the theme
steps.instruction: Create a function named provideTheme that uses Vue's provide API to make the theme object available to descendant components.
steps.hint: The provide function should take the theme object as a parameter and call provide with a key and the theme value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A provideTheme function is created that will share the theme with child components.
successCriteria: The provideTheme function is defined and uses the provide API with a key and theme parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function uses the provide API with both a key and the theme value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The provide function isn't quite right. Remember to create a function that calls provide with a key and the theme value.

steps.title: Create a component that injects the theme
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ThemeDisplay that uses inject to receive the theme object and returns a paragraph element showing the current theme value.
steps.hint:
Use the inject function from Vue to access the provided theme. The component should return a paragraph (

) element containing the theme value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ThemeDisplay component is created that uses inject to access the theme and displays it in a paragraph.
successCriteria: ThemeDisplay component is defined, uses inject to get the theme, and returns a paragraph element showing the theme value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your component uses inject to get the theme and returns a paragraph showing it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. Check that you're using inject to access the theme and returning a paragraph element.

steps.title: Display theme values in the child component
steps.instruction:
In the child component's template, add two

elements that display the theme's primaryColor and backgroundColor values.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to display reactive values in the template. Access the theme object you injected.
steps.analogousExample: // Displaying reactive values in template
steps.expectedOutcome: The child component will show the theme colors in the UI when rendered.
successCriteria: Two paragraph elements exist in the template, each displaying one theme property using {{ }} interpolation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial:
You're close. Make sure you have two separate

elements, each showing one theme property with {{ }}.
steps.feedbackWrong:
Check that you added two

elements in the template and used {{ theme.propertyName }} to display each color value.

steps.title: Create a button to toggle theme values
steps.instruction: In the ChildComponent template, add a button element with the text 'Toggle Theme' that will eventually toggle between light and dark themes.
steps.hint: Add a button element inside the template's div, similar to how you'd add any HTML button in Vue.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildComponent template now includes a button with the text 'Toggle Theme' that will be used in the next step to toggle theme colors.
successCriteria: A button element with the text 'Toggle Theme' is added inside the div in the ChildComponent template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a button element with the exact text 'Toggle Theme' inside the div in the ChildComponent template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element with text 'Toggle Theme' is missing from the ChildComponent template. Add it inside the div to proceed.

steps.title: Define a handler function for theme toggling
steps.instruction: Inside the ChildComponent's setup function, create a function named toggleTheme that toggles the theme.primaryColor between 'blue' and 'darkblue' and theme.backgroundColor between 'white' and 'black'.
steps.hint: Define a function that directly modifies the theme object's properties. Since theme is reactive, changes will automatically update the UI.
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleTheme function is defined inside the ChildComponent's setup function that switches the theme colors between light and dark values.
successCriteria: The toggleTheme function is defined and modifies both theme.primaryColor and theme.backgroundColor.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it toggles both theme.primaryColor and theme.backgroundColor between two values each.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleTheme function is not defined correctly. It should be inside the setup function and modify both color properties.

steps.title: Wire the button to the toggle handler
steps.instruction: Add a click event listener to the button in ChildComponent's template that calls the toggleTheme function.
steps.hint: In Vue templates, use @click to attach a click event handler to an element. The handler should be a function defined in the component's setup.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring a button to a handler
<button @click="handleClick">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button in ChildComponent's template will have a click event listener attached that calls the toggleTheme function when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element in the template includes @click="toggleTheme".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the button's click event is properly connected to the toggleTheme function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button click event isn't properly wired to the toggleTheme function. Check the template syntax for event listeners.

steps.title: Observe reactive updates in the child component
steps.instruction: In the ChildComponent template, update the two paragraphs to display the current theme.primaryColor and theme.backgroundColor values that will change when the button is clicked.
steps.hint: Use the theme object injected in setup() to access its properties in the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The child component will show the current theme colors, and clicking the button will demonstrate reactive updates as the displayed values change.
successCriteria: The template contains two paragraphs that display theme.primaryColor and theme.backgroundColor using Vue template syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added paragraphs, but make sure they display the actual theme properties using {{ theme.primaryColor }} and {{ theme.backgroundColor }}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraphs should display the theme values. Check that you're using the theme object from setup() in the template syntax.

steps.title: Mount the Vue application to the DOM
steps.instruction: Create a Vue app instance using createApp, provide the theme using provideTheme, and mount it to a DOM element with id 'app'.
steps.hint: Call createApp with a root component that uses provideTheme in its setup function, then call mount('#app') on the returned app instance.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue application will be fully set up and mounted to the DOM, making the theme context available to all child components.
successCriteria: The Vue app is created with createApp, uses provideTheme in its setup, and is mounted to '#app'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling createApp with a component that uses provideTheme, and mounting it to '#app'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Vue app isn't properly mounted. Check that you're using createApp and mount('#app').
